questions.text: Consider a disk pack with a seek time of 4 milliseconds and rotational speed of 10000 rotations per minute (RPM). It has 600 sectors per track and each sector can store 512 bytes of data. Consider a file stored in the disk. The file contains 2000 sectors. Assume that every sector access necessitates a seek, and the average rotational latency for accessing each sector is half of the time for one complete rotation. The total time (in milliseconds) needed to read the entire file is ____________.
questions.solution:
One rotation = 60 / 10000 s = 6 ms.

Per sector: seek 4 + latency 3 + transfer 6/600 = 0.01 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 7.01 ms

Total = 2000 [latex]\times[/latex] 7.01 = 14020 ms

Answer: 14020

questions.text:
For computers based on three-address instruction formats, each address field can be used to specify which of the following:
(S1) A memory operand
(S2) A processor register
(S3) An implied accumulator register
questions.solution:
In a three-address instruction, each address field explicitly names a memory location or a register. An implied accumulator is used only in one-address formats.

Answer: Either S1 or S2

questions.text: Assume that 16-bit CPU is trying to access a double word stating at an odd address. How many memory operations are required to access the data?
questions.solution:
A 16-bit CPU reads 2 bytes per memory operation, at even (aligned) addresses. A double word (4 bytes) starting at an odd address covers 3 aligned words: one partial, one full and one partial.

So 3 memory operations are needed.

Answer: 3

questions.text: Suppose you want to build a memory with 4 byte words and a capacity of [latex]2^{21}[/latex] bits. What is type of decoder required if the memory is built using [latex]2K \times 8[/latex] RAM chips?
questions.solution:
One word = 32 bits needs 4 chips (each 8 bits wide) in a row. One row holds 2K words = [latex]2^{11}\times32=2^{16}[/latex] bits.

Rows = [latex]2^{21}/2^{16}=32[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] a 5-to-32 decoder selects the row.

Answer: 5 to 32

questions.text: If each address space represents one byte of storage space, how many address lines are needed to access RAM chips arranged in a [latex]4 \times 6[/latex] array, where each chip is [latex]8K \times 4[/latex] bits ?
questions.solution:
Total = 4 [latex]\times[/latex] 6 chips [latex]\times[/latex] 8K [latex]\times[/latex] 4 bits = 768K bits = 96 KB.

Byte addressing: [latex]2^{16}=64K\lt 96K\le 2^{17}[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 17 address lines.

Answer: 17
